svg.title: What did not work
svg.desc: Six approaches that did not pay off, with the reason: hardware decode inside headless Chrome, capturing only the changed area, Remotion's removed Experimental.Clipper, shared-memory capture with NVENC for graphics, ProRes or VP9 alpha for the graphics layer, and running several ffmpeg segments at once.
svg.text: Each one measured or tried on video R. CPU seconds where there is a number.

g.text: VA-API decoder opens, then the GPU process crashes
when the frame goes to compositing. dec stays at 0%.
Capture only the area that changed
Capture −19 s, but recomposing in Node costs 32.4 s against
8.1 s for ffmpeg to decode full PNGs. 816 of 2241 frames not pixel-exact.
Removed by Remotion because it “did not actually make the render
faster, rather slower”. Our dirty-rect prototype agrees.
renderMedia straight to h264_nvenc for the graphics layer
costs more CPU than writing a PNG sequence.
Encoding the graphics layer costs far more than the
decode it saves: ProRes +86.8 s, VP9 +20.0 s.
Two jobs: wall clock −28%, CPU +20%, +1.3 GB VRAM.
Kept as an option, off by default.
